name: Mr. Gyro's
address: 1100 S. Martin Luther King Jr. Dr.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed raw chicken being stored above raw fish, and raw fish being stored above ready-to-eat foods (sauces and sliced peppers) in the 2-door stacked standing cooler and the bottom of the prep cooler. CORRECTED: The raw chicken was moved below the raw fish, and the ready-to-eat foods were moved to a separate part of the prep cooler so that they were not stored below raw meat. Inspector and PIC discussed keeping meat in separate doors of the prep cooler. Ensure that raw meats are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods, and that meats are stored in order of final cooking temperature, with the highest temperature on the bottom: fish & shrimp & eggs (135 F), whole intact beef and pork (145 F), ground beef and pork (155 F), and chicken and poultry (165 F) always on the bottom.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed several food items stored inside the 3-door standing cooler that were well above the cold holding temperature of 41°F. CORRECTED: PIC and Inspectors checked all food items with a calibrated stem thermometer and either discarded items or moved items to working coolers: 
- items that were too warm and were prepared outside of the safe cooling time window were discarded; 
- items that were still cooling inside the safe cooling time window were moved to working coolers to continue cooling.
Items voluntarily discarded included: ~6 containers of raw chicken (47-52°F), 2 containers of raw steak (52°F), a 2 containers of cooked chicken (49-85°F), and 3 small containers of cooked potatoes (50°F).
PIC will work on getting the 3-door standing cooler repaired (see Violation #33) and will confirm with Inspector before resuming food service in the cooler. Ensure that all TCS Foods are cold held at temperatures of 41°F or less.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed the 3-door standing cooler was no longer cooling or cold holding, with several food items measured at temperatures above 41°F. PIC and Inspectors checked all food items with a stem thermometer and discarded or moved items as determined by temperature and cooling time (see Violation #22). Inspector will Follow Up to check the progress of repairing the 3-door standing cooler. Cease all food storage in the 3-door standing cooler until Inspector can confirm the cooler is effectively cooling and cold holding food. Ensure that all equipment for cooling and cold holding is sufficient in capacity to provide temperatures below 41°F.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw seafood stored over various packages of produce in the walk-in cooler. The raw seafood was moved onto the bottom shelf during the inspection. The PIC was provided with educational handouts which the inspector recommends hanging by the walk-in cooler. Ensure that raw meats are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed a knife stored between the prep cooler lids. Since the surface between the lids is not routinely cleaned and sanitized storing the knife there presents the risk of contamination. During the inspection the knife was removed for cleaning. Inspector and PIC discussed storing the knife in a new location. Ensure that food preparation utensils are always clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed single-use knives by the front cash register stored with the handles and food contact portions intermixed. During the inspection the knives were inverted so that the handles were all facing outwards. Ensure that single-use utensils are always stored to prevent contamination of the food contact surface.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned:

(1) The accumulation of dust on the internal fans of the silver triple door cooler, stacked cooler, walk-in cooler, and walk-in freezer. 

(2) The debris on the bottom of the container holding clean utensils between the triple sink and grill.

(3) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The accumulation of grease and food residue underneath the grill. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Observed the following lacked date marking when the inspector arrived at the facility:

(1) Rice that was cooked yesterday morning in the silver triple door cooler.
(2) Rice that was cooked yesterday morning in the walk-in cooler. 
(2) Gyro meat that was cooked and cooled on Sunday in the walk-in cooler. 

During the inspection the above referenced foods were correctly date marked. The PIC was reminded that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was prepared/opened being day one; food is discarded after six additional days). Ensure that all required foods are properly date marked by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed bare wood planks on the wall behind the slushy machines by the cash register. The bare wood must be sealed (ex.painted) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

The PIC began the process of cleaning the surface during the inspection. Ensure that underneath the grills remains clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed there is a missing cover on the light switch to the left of the mop sink closet. Ensure that the missing cover is replaced to maintain physical facilities in good repair by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed a personal drink stored on the shelf above the prep cooler on the cookline. The drink was removed from the shelf during the inspection. Ensure that personal drinks are stored away from food preparation areas to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed that the PIC’s allergen awareness training expired in May 2025. The PIC will be renewing their certificate. Ensure that all CFPM’s have training in allergen awareness principles by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a cutting board stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. The PIC was educated that the cutting board could become contaminated by dirty water splashes stored in this position. The PIC removed the cutting board from behind the faucet and moved it to another location. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always stored away from sources of contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces:

(1) The bare wood planks on the wall by the cash register behind the slushy machines. The bare wood must be sealed (ex.painted) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface.

(2) The gap between the order window in the customer area and the kitchen is filled with foam. The gap must be filled to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface.

Ensure that the above referenced are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned: 

(1) THIIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION - Observed there were drips on the hood system above the grills and fryers. These drips pose a risk of contaminating food cooking below. The portions of the hood system over the grills and fryers must be cleaned often enough to avoid the accumulation of drips. The PIC cleaned the drips during the inspection (COS).

(2) The shelves for drying clean dishes over the triple sink have an accumulation of grease from the adjacent grills and fryers. The dirty shelves pose the risk of contaminating clean dishes. The shelves must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of grease. 

Ensure that the above referenced non-food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch by at next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed several times during the inspection employees did not wash hands before donning gloves or switching gloves. The PIC was informed that hands must be washed using the proper hand washing procedure before donning gloves. The inspector will follow-up on 3/6/2025 to ensure that employees are washing hands before donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed the steam table was not holding foods at 135F or above. The steam table had an internal temperature of 122F in the front, 114F in the middle, and 112F in the back. The inspector noticed that the knob was turned on a low setting. After being informed the PIC turned up the steam table to a higher setting. When the inspector re-checked the internal temperatures at the end of the inspection they were at 142F in the front, 149F in the middle, and 150F in the back. The PIC was reminded to check the temperatures of the steam table on a regular basis. Ensure that temperature control for safety foods hot holding are always maintained at 135F or above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: THIS IS A THREE TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed several temperature controlled for safety (TCS), ready-to-eat foods at the facility for longer than 24 hours were not date marked: (1) Desserts (candy covered grapes, cheesecake, and banana pudding) in the clear triple cooler; (2) Several large containers of par-cooked chicken wings in the stacked double cooler; (3) Containers of cut onions and tomatoes, shredded lettuce, cooked rice, and par-cooked chicken wings in the triple cooler; (4) Cooked gyro meat in the prep cooler bottom; and (5) Several large containers of par-cooked chicken wings in the walk-in cooler. The PIC stated that all the above referenced foods had been inside the coolers since at least yesterday (therefore over 24 hours). The PIC date marked all the foods during the inspection. The inspector educated that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods held at the establishment longer than 24 hours must be date marked. The inspector will follow-up on 3/13/2025 to ensure that all required foods are date marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed that the bleach at the facility does not have an EPA registration. The inspector discussed the importance of using food contact surface sanitizing bleach in the facility. The inspector will follow-up on 3/6/2025 to ensure that the facility has bleach with an EPA registration.
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a container of raw beef was thawing in a container of water at room temperature when the inspector arrived. The PIC was educated that foods thawed using water must be thawed under continuous running water. The PIC placed the container holding the raw meat under continuous water in the triple sink during the inspection. The PIC was reminded of the approved thawing methods: (1) Within a cooler at 41F or below; (2) Under continuous running water; (3) As part of the cooking process; or (4) In the microwave. Ensure that foods are always thawed according to an approved method.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

The PIC was educated that the hood system must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of drips that can contaminate food cooking below. The PIC cleaned the drips off the hood system during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are kept clean of grease deposits and other soil accumulations.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed a cutting board stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. The cutting board could be contaminated by dirty water splashes or food debris in this position. The PIC was educated and the cutting board was moved to a different location. The cutting board must always be stored in a position that does not pose the risk of contamination to ensure it remains clean to sight and touch. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed several foods (including, but not limited too, cut green peppers, cut onions, beef, and chicken in the triple cooler and banana pudding, candy covered grapes, and cheesecake in the front dessert cooler) lacking proper date marking. The PIC was educated about the proper date marking procedure. Ensure that foods kept at the facility for longer than 24-hours are date marked to indicate the 7-day maximum. The day the food was prepared/opened is day 1. Food must be discarded after 7-days. The date marking must clearly indicate the food preparation and/or the discard date. The inspector will follow-up on 11/07/2024 to check on date marking. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Observed chicken thawing in the triple sink basin submerged in water but without continuous running water. The chicken was thawing in all three basins of the triple sink but there is only one faucet available. The inspector instructed the PIC to move the chicken into one basin to ensure all of the chicken is under continuous running water. An educational handout about the proper thawing procedure was provided to the PIC. Ensure that food is always thawed according to the proper thawing procedures (i.e., thawing food completely submerged under running water or inside coolers).

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed there are not test strips at the facility. The facility requires chlorine test strips to test their bleach sanitizer solutions. Ensure there is always test strips available to accurately measure the concentration of sanitizing solutions. The inspector will follow-up on 11/07/2024 to check that the facility has chlorine test strips. 

4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment:
3-201.11: Observed chocolate coated grapes prepared for sale (in a frontline cooler) purchased from an unapproved source. Owner stated that the grapes were being made by a friend, but now he will make them in-house. Grapes were removed from service during the inspection. Make foods within the store or buy from reputable sources. No homemade foods may be purchased for sale in your permitted kitchen. 

(A)-(B) FOOD shall be obtained from APPROVED source and not from private home. P (C) PACKAGED Food shall be properly labeled.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Overall, the facility has made drastic improvements since the last routine inspection. Most surfaces are observed clean, however, areas under the cooking equipment (between base of equipment and tabletop) and within the fryers are observed to have an accumulation of grease. There is significant ponding of grease beneath the cooking equipment. See that equipment is cleaned. 

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed the PIC could not locate signed employee reporting agreements. The inspectors provided blank copies of the employee reporting agreements to the PIC. There will be a follow-up on 07/22/2024 to ensure there are signed copies of the employee reporting forms for all employees.

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Observed there was not a written procedure for employees to follow when responding to vomit or diarrheal events at the facility. A written procedure was given to the PIC during the inspection. There is sufficient bleach at the facility to respond to events. Ensure that the written procedure is always available at the facility and that bleach continue to be sufficient. 

2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink and bathroom sink do not have signs notifying employees that they must wash their hands before returning to work. The inspectors provided the PIC with handwashing signs and they were posted at the sinks during the inspection. Ensure that all hand sinks always have signs notifying employees that they must wash their hands before returning to work.

6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed raw marinated chicken and beef stored above onions and potatoes in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was provided a handout about correct storage order and moved the raw meat below the produce during the inspection. Ensure that food is always stored according to their correct storage order.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed the following food needs date-marking: (1) Par chicken in the walk-in cooler (REPEAT VIOLATION); and (2) Banana pudding and cheese-cake in the front standing cooler. Discussed date-marking with the PIC and provided a handout. Ensure that all containers not used within 24-hours are date marked to avoid food being held for longer than 7-days. There will be a follow-up on 07/22/2024 to ensure proper date-marking. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Observed the triple standing cooler, walk-in cooler, and the stacked double coolers do not have thermometers. Ensure that all refrigerated food storage units have temperature measuring devices to measure the air temperature. There will be a follow-up on 07/22/2024 to ensure that the triple standing cooler, walk-in cooler, and stacked double coolers have thermometers. 

4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed roaches at multiple locations (including but not limited too: grease storage unit, mop sink, triple sink, within boxes of packaged food, and front service area) and a dead mouse in a trap in the furnace room. Ensure that the premise is maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The facility will need to get pest control to eliminate pests. There will be a follow-up every two weeks for the at least the next 30-days to ensure the pest issue is decreasing/eliminated and to show proof of pest control. The first follow-up will be on 07/22/2024.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed food (including but not limited to, mushrooms and salsa) being stored in cardboard boxes on the floor in the dry-storage area next to the walk-in cooler. Ensure that all food is protected from contamination by being at least 6-inches above the floor.

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT..

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed clean single-use articles (including, but not limited to, aluminum pans and to-go containers) stored in boxes on the ground in the back adjacent to the walk-in cooler. Ensure that all clean single-use articles are stored at lease 6-inches off the ground to prevent contamination. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed several drips on the hood system over the cook line. Drips pose a threat of contamination to cooking foods. Ensure that all non-food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil. The PIC wiped off the drips during the inspection. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed personal food (veggie salad) stored on the top-shelf in the walk-in cooler. Ensure that all personal foods are located below or away from food intended for consumers to avoid contamination. The PIC threw away the personal food during the inspection. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Multiple containers of par cooked wings were observed in the triple door cooler unlabeled.  Discussed with PIC, who stated the wings are not held longer than 2 days.  Ensure all the containers that are not used within 24 hrs are date marked to avoid foods being held longer than 7 days.  

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
Multiple plastic to-go containers were observed in the clear door cooler containing various cakes without labeling.  Discussed with PIC.  When packaging bulk foods from their original container, ensure the new container is clearly marked with its contents.  The original label from the bulk container can also be stored in a binder or clear sleeve listing all ingredients and allergen information for customers as long as the to-go containers are labeled appropriately.

3-602.11: (A) FOOD PACKAGED in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be properly labeled. (B) Regulatory requirements-(1) The common name of the FOOD/identity statement; 106 (2) List ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, declaration of artificial colors and flavors and chemical preservatives; (3) net contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (5) MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS. Pf (6) Nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling UNLESS EXEMPT Under FDCA. (Pf) (C) Bulk FOOD for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be labeled in plain view. (D) Bulk, unPACKAGED FOODS portioned for CONSUMERS shall be properly labeled.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S)

Hood cleaning being performed within the facility is not sufficient to prevent the accumulation of dust and residue. Dust and residue is hanging/dripping from the baffles of the hood which has the potential to lead to food contamination when foods are cooked underneath. Further, improperly maintained and cleaned hoods pose a fire hazard to the facility if allowed to worsen. Ensure that the hood is cleaned often enough to prevent oil and dust from building up on the baffles. The frequency of cleaning must be increased to accomodate the amount of foods cooked underneath the hood. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed ceiling tile which are water damaged and/or misplaced. Replace the damaged/misplaced ceiling tile to ensure that the ceiling remains smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Operator indicated that the property owner has been notified of the leaking ceiling resulting in damaged ceiling tile. Leaks must be repaired by the next routine inspection to prevent further damage and potential contamination of foods stored underneath. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a staff member touch an ear bud, put gloves on, and continue working with food. Hands must be washed ANY TIME contamination may have occurred.

Work with ALL staff to ensure compliance with hand washing procedure and frequency. Procedure includes a) wasing hands for AT LEAST 20 seconds b) using soap and warm water c) turning off the faucet with a paper towel as a barrier between the hands and the knob on the faucet. 

Inspector observed operator educating staff members of hand washing and education has been provided. Corrected on site. No follow-up required at this time.

If hand washing signage in a language beside English would be helpful to ensure compliance, contact your inspector immediately and materials will be provided. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Inspector provided education to operator regarding accessiblity of hand sinks within the facility. The facility is small and provides limited space for food preparation activities. During the spot-check, inspector observed a staff member preparing meat patties at a short table immediately next to the hand sink with the employee sitting on a stool directly in front of the hand sink blocking access. 

Hand sinks must be available for employees to wash their hands at all times with no exceptions. Hand sinks cannot be used for any purposes apart from hand washing. Hand sinks must remain stocked with paper towels and appropriate hand soap at all times. 

During the inspection, operator had food preparation moved from immediately in front of the sink to adjacent to the sink. This is not ideal because hand washing activities will result in water spray potentially contaminating the food. Work with staff and determine a better location for preparing meat in the facility moving forward and ensure that hand sinks remain accessible during all operational hours. Coach staff on appropriate locations for food preparation.

If signage in a language beside English would be helpful for ensuring compliance with hand washing requirements, reach out to your inspector immediately and materials will be provided to assist with compliance. 

The hand sink was stocked and accessible at the end of the spot-check today. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed a food employee switch gloves and switch acivities without hand washing. Educate employees on proper timing for hand washing including anytime gloves are changed and any time that changes in activities occur, especially when switching from raw food (fries) to ready-to-eat food (gyro meat). Work with all staff to increase the frequency of hand washing within the facility. A follow-up will be issued for 10-days on 4/24/2023 to evaluate hand washing frequency and procedure. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION.

Sliced tomatoes in the prep cooler were observed to be between 45 and 50 degrees F. Chopped lettuce in the prep cooler was observed to be 45 to 50 degrees F. Individual containers of ranch dressing were being held at 50 degrees in the coke upright cooler. These items are all TCS items and must be time/temperature controlled for safety. All cold held items MUST be held at 41 degrees F or below. During lunch hours, these items become heated as a result of proximity to hot equipment especially gyro spit directing heat towards the prep cooler. Work with staff to ensure the lid remains closed on the pre cooler. Remove a portion of the soda from the coke upright cooler to allow for proper circulation. Monitor temperatures closely.

A follow-up is being issued for 10-days. Inspector will return on 04/24/2023 to evaluate compliance with cold holding temperatures.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

Ensure that mops are stored properly between uses such as hanging inverted along the wall or in the top portion of the mop bucket as discussed.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: Employee health reporting agreement was not on file with the establishment during the inspection. New copies of the reporting agreement was given during the inspection and the purpose of the paperwork was explained to the PIC.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: Norovirus cleanup procedure was not on file with the establishment during the inspection. A new copy with a stressed educational session on the importance of knowing how to properly clean up Norovirus was provided to the facility. Ensure this document is kept on file with the facility.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Food items in the standing fridge were observed to be uncovered with employee materials stored above it. This was brought to the PIC's attention and a lid was placed on the storage container. Ensure a lid remains on the container when not in use in order to eliminate potential contamination threats.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: Prep cooler items were observed to be warmer than the allowed 41 degrees F. The lid was left open for an extended period of time. This was brought to the cook's attention and the lids were closed. Being the items were exposed at those temperatures less than 4 hours, no items were thrown away during inspection. Ensure the lid remains closed to limit ambient air exposure to assist the cooler and the food items to remain at proper temperature.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: Items in the standing fridge were observed to not be date marked. PIC was made aware of the situation and stated the items were prepped yesterday and will be used within 48-72 hours. Education was provided to inform the PIC that any item over 24 hours in the restaurant needs to be properly date marked with the date of preparation. Dates are being added to the food items during inspection. Ensure this practice continues to maintain the integrity of the food being served.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: No active thermometers were observed to be in place in the standing fridges or freezers. Ensure thermometers are purchased and placed in the warmest part of the coolers to ensure the integrity of the food through temperature control.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: Scoops were observed to have their handles being stored in the dry material. The cook was made aware of this issue and removed the scoops and replaced them with scoops that can store the handles appropriately without risking contamination from hands. Ensure this practice continues to reduce risk of contamination. 
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.
